title: LabOS System Architecture
section: Skill-driven scientific runtime and distributed execution
note: This redesigned LabOS architecture uses three interchangeable PC symbols for an arbitrary fleet, with no fixed assignment of scientific functions to PCs. One central LabOS server hosts scientific AI reasoning, specialist sub-agents, knowledge and memory, a skill library, MCP host/client components and tool connectors, a capability registry, and deterministic coordination. A server-side model router prefers a remote cloud model and falls back to the server's local LLM when cloud connectivity, the API or its quota is unavailable. The agents preserve experiment context and tool permissions across model changes. Each instrument-host PC runs one persistent execution worker, called a PC Agent. The worker does not require a local large language model. It owns instrument sessions, bounded adapters, a command journal, watchdog and artifact outbox. An operator computer can use only a browser. All laboratory PCs initiate their HTTP(S) connections; command arrows represent payload flow, not inbound network sessions. Physical device interfaces remain local to the instrument host. Skills package reusable scientific procedures and supporting references or scripts. MCP exposes tools, resources and prompts; the LabOS control connector routes instrument actions through the deterministic coordinator. Hardware reference and trigger cables are separate from this control network. This figure describes the scalable LabOS system design, rather than an inventory of currently commissioned drivers.
